result:
I fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings. Afterwards I re-ran a script that compares all 150 rules against what their docstrings say, over a grid of quantities and unit prices, and every rule now matches.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | Cap was applied to the price instead of the discount (`min(base, 30000) * 5 // 100`) | Work out the discount first, then cap it |
| 15 | A "whole" rule was calculating like a "marginal" one (only units over 10) | Use the whole order (`base * 10 // 100`) |
| 27 | Started at 101 units instead of 100 | `qty >= 100` |
| 40 | Cap only applied once the discount went over 60,000 | Always cap at 30,000 |
| 46 | Gave 4% instead of 3% | Changed to 3% |
| 47 | `round` instead of rounding down | `// 100` |
| 55 | Cap only applied once the discount went over 200,000 | Always cap at 100,000 |
| 59 | Gave 3% instead of 2% | Changed to 2% |
| 106 | Started at 6 units instead of 5 (`qty > 5`) | `qty >= 5` |
| 107 | Started at 51 units instead of 50 (`qty > 50`) | `qty >= 50` |
| 124 | A "whole" rule was calculating like a "marginal" one | Use the whole order (`base * 7 // 100`) |

Rule 136 also says `qty > 5`, but it's a marginal rule, so the discount at exactly 5 units is 0 either way. It already behaves as documented, so I didn't change it.

STATUS: DONE
